title: Nim — 28 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Nim. 28 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/nim.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 10 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 18 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 5 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 191 pairs; the theorems fall into 2 strands, the largest of 27. Most binding: xorN (18), xorF (7), N (5), isLost (4), grundy1 (2). 1 theorem names no definition of the file and stands on its own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: fnv.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/nim.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 28 sealed receipts fold to c002124f-d671-8e3f-8609-9335b0759a96. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (6, 2, 5, 1, 2, 1, 3). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: flow.lean (3 observed, 1.22 expected, lift 2.46), rights.lean (4 observed, 1.95 expected, lift 2.05), index.lean (5 observed, 2.68 expected, lift 1.87). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.46 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 54.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.33; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.58. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 088ec1cc76f5 (2026-09-15), over 806 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Nim — Charles L. Bouton, 1901; the Sprague–Grundy theorem — Roland Sprague, 1935 and Patrick M. Grundy, 1939. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. bouton_two_heaps_lost_iff_xor_zero — (List.range N).all (fun a => (List.range N).all (fun b => isLost a b == (xorN a b == 0))) record
  2. bouton_lost_iff_heaps_equal — (List.range N).all (fun a => (List.range N).all (fun b => isLost a b == (a == b))) record
  3. lost_positions_are_exactly_the_diagonal — (((List.range N).flatMap (fun a => (List.range N).map (fun b => (a, b)))).filter (fun p => isLost p.1 p.2)).length = N record
  4. grundy_of_a_single_heap_is_its_size — (List.range N).all (fun n => grundy1 (n + 1) n == n) record
  5. grundy_of_two_heaps_is_the_xor — (List.range N).all (fun a => (List.range N).all (fun b => (xorN (grundy1 (a + 1) a) (grundy1 (b + 1) b)) == xorN a b)) record
  6. xor_is_its_own_inverse — (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN (xorN a b) b == a)) record
  7. xor_is_commutative — (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN a b == xorN b a)) record
  8. xor_zero_is_identity — (List.range 32).all (fun a => xorN a 0 == a) record
  9. the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition — (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN a b == xorN b a)) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => (List.range 16).all (fun c => xorN (xorN a b) c == xorN a (xorN b c)))) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN (xorN a b) b == a)) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a => xorN a 0 == a) record
  10. bouton_holds_at_every_heap_size_to_six — (List.range 7).all (fun a => (List.range 7).all (fun b => isLost a b == (xorN a b == 0))) record
  11. the_xor_of_two_bits_is_their_sum_mod_two — ∀ x y : Nat, (if x % 2 == y % 2 then 0 else 1) = (x + y) % 2 record
  12. xor_commutes_at_every_fuel — ∀ f a b : Nat, xorF f a b = xorF f b a record
  13. one_more_step_of_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument — ∀ f a b : Nat, (a < f ∨ b < f) → xorF (f + 1) a b = xorF f a b record
  14. more_fuel_changes_nothing_once_it_exceeds_an_argument — ∀ k f a b : Nat, (a < f ∨ b < f) → xorF (f + k) a b = xorF f a b record
  15. xor_reads_the_same_at_every_sufficient_fuel — ∀ g a b : Nat, (a < g ∨ b < g) → xorN a b = xorF g a b record
  16. a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_at_every_fuel — ∀ f b : Nat, xorF f b b = 0 record
  17. xor_splits_off_its_lowest_bit — ∀ g x c : Nat, 1 ≤ g → xorF (g + 1) x c = (x + c) % 2 + 2 * xorF g (x / 2) (c / 2) record
  18. xor_undoes_itself_when_the_fuel_suffices — ∀ f a b g : Nat, (a < f ∨ b < f) → b < g → xorF g (xorF f a b) b = a record
  19. xor_is_commutative_for_every_a_b — ∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b = xorN b a record
  20. xor_zero_is_identity_for_every_a — ∀ a : Nat, xorN a 0 = a record
  21. xor_is_its_own_inverse_for_every_a_b — ∀ a b : Nat, xorN (xorN a b) b = a record
  22. xor_is_the_sum_of_the_bits_plus_twice_the_xor_of_the_halves — ∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b = (a + b) % 2 + 2 * xorN (a / 2) (b / 2) record
  23. xor_is_associative_below_every_bound — ∀ n a b c : Nat, a + b + c ≤ n → xorN (xorN a b) c = xorN a (xorN b c) record
  24. xor_is_associative_for_every_a_b_c — ∀ a b c : Nat, xorN (xorN a b) c = xorN a (xorN b c) record
  25. the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition_for_every_a_b_c — ∀ a b c : Nat, xorN a b = xorN b a ∧ xorN (xorN a b) c = xorN a (xorN b c) ∧ xorN (xorN a b) b = a ∧ xorN a 0 = a record
  26. a_number_xored_with_itself_is_zero_for_every_a — ∀ a : Nat, xorN a a = 0 record
  27. xor_is_zero_only_on_equal_arguments_for_every_a_b — ∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b = 0 ↔ a = b record
  28. the_halves_and_the_low_bit_read_back_from_the_xor_for_every_a_b — ∀ a b : Nat, xorN a b / 2 = xorN (a / 2) (b / 2) ∧ xorN a b % 2 = (a + b) % 2 record

Recompute. Clone https://github.com/ceccec/millennium-solutions at commit 088ec1cc76f5 and run npm ci && npm run lean, which checks every Lean file in dependency order. This record was generated by scripts/clusters.ts from the source and the ledger.
